statusDetail: Atomic coverage complete: 58/58 checks judged across six representative paths. Authenticated editing, account creation, revision history, donation completion and locale variants were not covered because they require credentials, consequential actions, or duplicate templates.

page.notes: Public server-rendered encyclopedia. Root redirects to Wikipedia:Hauptseite. Representative coverage includes homepage, article, category, search, login and missing-article recovery.

paths.description: Public homepage: content hub, global navigation, appearance controls and search entry point.
Representative long-form encyclopedia article with infobox, media, table of contents and extensive links.
Primary find-content journey and results template, exercised with a non-exact query.
Representative account form and authentication entry point; empty submission exercised without credentials.
Representative failure/recovery state for a missing article.

findings.summary: The default appearance remains light when the OS requests dark mode.
findings.evidence: The prefers-color-scheme: dark screenshot is visually identical to the normal screenshot and the appearance panel shows “Hell” selected; “Automatisch” and “Dunkel” exist but are not the default.
findings.suggestedFix: Default anonymous users to the automatic color scheme, declare color-scheme: light dark, and retain the explicit override as a stored user choice.

findings.summary: Article and route changes are abrupt rather than using cross-document View Transitions.
findings.evidence: DOM/CSS probes found no view-transition rules while the representative site journey uses full-document article navigation.
findings.suggestedFix: Opt eligible same-origin navigations into cross-document View Transitions and disable non-essential motion under prefers-reduced-motion.

findings.summary: Menus use checkbox-driven, relatively positioned dropdowns rather than anchored popovers with fallback placement.
findings.evidence: The overlay probe found eight checkbox-controlled dropdowns, zero popover elements, zero dialogs/details, and relative positioning for the sticky-header table-of-contents dropdown.
findings.suggestedFix: Use popover for transient menus and CSS anchor positioning with position-try fallbacks, preserving a supported fallback.

findings.summary: Transient menus are implemented with checkbox controls rather than semantic light-dismiss primitives.
findings.evidence: The live DOM exposes checkbox toggles for main, appearance, user, language and tools menus but no popover, dialog or details elements.
findings.suggestedFix: Migrate transient menus to popover with declarative invokers and light-dismiss behavior; use dialog only for modal flows.

findings.summary: The desktop skin does not reflow at narrow window widths and instead forces a 1120px layout.
findings.evidence: At a requested 360x800 viewport the page declares meta viewport width=1120; layout evidence reports a 1120–1430 CSS-pixel viewport and screenshots show desktop columns and very small text scaled into 360px. Lighthouse with a mobile user agent receives the separate Minerva skin, so this specifically affects narrow desktop-UA windows and responsive emulation.
findings.suggestedFix: Replace the fixed width=1120 viewport with width=device-width and make the Vector skin reflow intrinsically; keep server-selected Minerva as an enhancement, not the only mobile path.

findings.summary: The homepage accessibility tree contains hidden focusable descendants and unnamed controls/links.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse accessibility scored 0.88 and reported eight aria-hidden-focus failures plus failures for an unlabeled control and a link without a discernible name.
findings.suggestedFix: Remove focusable descendants from aria-hidden containers, give every control/link a stable accessible name, and verify the accessibility tree and keyboard traversal.

findings.summary: The login flow forces a positive tabindex sequence and its mobile menu checkbox has no valid exposed label.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse found tabindex values 1, 2, 3, 7 and 100 on login controls and flagged the navigation checkbox because its referenced label is aria-hidden.
findings.suggestedFix: Remove positive tabindex values so DOM order controls focus, and expose a valid name on the menu control without hiding its label from assistive technology.

findings.summary: The homepage ships substantial JavaScript and CSS that Lighthouse identifies as unused.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse estimates 232 KiB unused JavaScript and 99 KiB unused CSS; HAR records 555,475 transferred script bytes across 11 requests, including a 323,285-byte loader response.
findings.suggestedFix: Split ResourceLoader modules by page need, delay editing/account modules until intent, and remove or scope unused homepage CSS.

findings.summary: Several large assets lack useful cache headers and one image lacks dimensions.
findings.evidence: The HAR summary lists multiple Wikimedia images without cache headers; Lighthouse also reports one unsized image, although measured CLS remained 0.
findings.suggestedFix: Apply durable immutable caching to versioned media and emit width/height or aspect-ratio for every content image.

findings.summary: Public homepage and article templates omit meta descriptions.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse SEO flags meta-description on the homepage; direct homepage and article metadata probes found titles and canonicals but no meta[name=description].
findings.suggestedFix: Generate concise, template-specific descriptions from the lead or page purpose while keeping titles and canonicals unique.

findings.summary: Article sharing metadata is incomplete and no structured-data block describes the entity.
findings.evidence: The Deutschland response provides og:title, og:type and og:image but no Open Graph description and no JSON-LD; homepage probe also reports jsonld: 0.
findings.suggestedFix: Add accurate Open Graph descriptions and an appropriate schema.org JSON-LD representation for encyclopedia articles, matching visible lead content.

findings.summary: Browser-enforced defenses are weakened by a broad CSP and absent anti-framing/referrer/permissions policies.
findings.evidence: Header evidence shows CSP script-src allows unsafe-inline and unsafe-eval across a very broad origin list; no frame-ancestors or X-Frame-Options, Referrer-Policy, or Permissions-Policy was present. HSTS and nosniff were present.
findings.suggestedFix: Move toward nonce/hash-based CSP without unsafe-eval, add frame-ancestors, and define explicit Referrer-Policy and Permissions-Policy headers.

findings.summary: Anonymous-session cookies use SameSite=None broadly and one session identifier is not Secure.
findings.evidence: Cookie evidence found six cookies with SameSite=None and dewikimwuser-sessionId without Secure or HttpOnly; Lighthouse separately observed three third-party-cookie uses during central auth/resource requests. The tested identifier was not proven to be an authentication credential.
findings.suggestedFix: Use Lax/Strict by default, reserve SameSite=None; Secure for necessary cross-site flows, and mark every session identifier Secure (and HttpOnly unless JavaScript access is essential).

findings.summary: The login surface logs a manifest parse error, misses source maps and blocks BFCache.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse reports a web app manifest syntax error on auth.wikimedia.org, missing/invalid maps for large first-party JavaScript, inspector cookie issues, and one BFCache prevention reason.
findings.suggestedFix: Serve a valid manifest response, repair ResourceLoader source maps, resolve inspector cookie warnings and remove the identified BFCache blocker.

findings.summary: Submitting the empty login form gives focus but no visible or announced required-field explanation.
findings.evidence: After activating Anmelden with both fields empty, the captured state only focuses the username field; there is no required marker, inline error text, or visible summary, and the DOM probe reports required=false and no aria-invalid.
findings.suggestedFix: Mark required fields semantically and, after submission, show and announce concise field-level feedback while preserving focus and entered values.
